failure_or_lesson: Cancelling an async await cannot terminate a synchronous inference adapter or a driver thread. Inference needs a terminable process; passive reads need fresh owned bounded connections and must never reconcile after cancellation. Current Claim/state/artifact authority cannot by itself preserve a before judgment after a genuine after update: frozen semantic phase routing is still required while consent stays current. Same-evidence general-model output is not an update-exclusion ablation. A phase grant can disappear during private metadata I/O, so each inner receipt decryption needs its own current gate. Cancelling an asyncio wrapper is not physical driver-thread completion: use the actual concurrent future for slot ownership and prevent same-task encoder retries from opening a second invocation. A standalone phase metadata checker is insufficient if the actual fresh reader continues to use current runtime heads: bind the actual selected phase runtime and lineage together. A snapshot containing the run digest cannot also put its own payload/event hashes into that digest; predeclare its immutable identity and authenticate its exact bytes through custody. Fixture deadline expansion does not qualify performance. A phase-history controller using the same permission object being fenced can recursively call itself; copy its current original permission reader before applying the runtime gate and keep both on the same owned selected connection. Phase archive custody needs an exact authenticated artifact permission route independent of generic original-only model context. A guarded reader deliberately bypasses overridable object instance methods, so no-open tests must observe the actual ciphertext backend or AEAD boundary. A four-operation archived native fixture performed tens of thousands of selected metadata reads for roughly one hundred physical ciphertext reads. Repeated full phase lineage/context construction and nested permission fences dominate; crypto itself does not explain the delay. Deduplicate only already authenticated operation-local work, preserve fresh uncached authority boundaries, and require actual selected-backend measurements before claiming latency. A final run digest cannot be known before observing its captures: use an earlier actual preregistration anchor, then seal observed body/event references into the later final plan. An optional authority parameter must not downgrade a durably anchored run to legacy execution. Full seal qualification is an outer passive operation; recursively reopening every producer proof inside each proof decrypt is invalid, while a metadata guard alone cannot authorize dispatch or acceptance. A source-policy object shared by a model-context gate and final/controller custody can deny legitimate controls or recurse when mutated: clone the scoped model view and retain independently current original predicates. Embedded-loop cross-thread wakeups can wait for a distant timer after cancellation; keep bounded polling active without freeing physical ownership early. A synchronous final-seal SELECT before the task deadline can block the async loop despite later async guards. Actual metadata must use owned bounded passive readers. Small synchronous writes also need physical PGconn bounds and exclusive ownership; a timeout option or detached shared writer thread is insufficient. A retained socket watchdog must disarm after success, preserve owner-thread driver closure, poison failure ownership, and keep unrelated callback deadline qualifications explicit.
